Standards may be approved by ANSI only after ANSI has verified that the requirements for due process, consensus and other criteria have been met in the development process. ANSI World Wide Web

question: The ANSI/AIHA Z10, American National Standard for Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems purpose is to:
options: Establish performance criteria for management acceptance of risk to employees and the public
Establish a tool for continual improvement of occupational safety and health performance
Establish a tool to assist organizations with regulatory compliance
Establish a minimum level of performance for organization health and safety programs in the international environment
explanation: The ANSI/AIHA Z10, American National Standard for Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems purpose is to establish a tool for continual improvement of occupational safety and health performance. ANSI/AIHA Z10-2005

question: The ANSI/AIHA Z10, American National Standard for Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems concept is based on the recognized quality concept of:
explanation: The ANSI/AIHA Z10, American National Standard for Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems concept is based on the recognized quality concept of plan, do, check, act. ANSI/AIHA Z10-2005

question: In manual materials handling, methods for eliminating the need to bend include all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Using lift tables, work dispensers, and other mechanical aids
Raising the work level to an appropriate height
Providing materials and tools in front of the worker
explanation: Although providing materials and tools in front of the worker helps to prevent twisting motions, to avoid bending motions the work needs to be at the proper height. This can be accomplished through mechanical means (lift tables), raising the work level, or lowering the worker to the level of the work.

question: Human factors engineering or ergonomics is concerned with fitting the worker to a task or the task to the worker. A man/machine system is considered a closed loop system. Which one of the following does NOT make up the closed loop system?
explanation: The closed loop system is made up of reactions, machine, data input, and senses of man.

question: Human factors engineering is fitting the worker to the task or the task to the worker. Man is better at all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Sensitive to a wide variety of stimuli
explanation: Machines are better at exerting large forces smoothly.

question: Human factors engineering is a technical discipline which concerns any of the following EXCEPT:
options: Design of the workplace to reduce mistakes and accidents
Design of tools to promote comfort
explanation: Human factors, also referred to as ergonomics, human engineering, bioengineering, and biomedics is a technical discipline mainly concerned with optimizing the relationship between people AND their work environment.

question: A safety program begins by:
options: Assuring compliance with all OSHA standards
Soliciting support of the facilities department
explanation: Management must develop a policy statement that clearly defines management's support for safety and the safety-related roles of each member of the organization.

question: When an employee's exposure to an airborne, breathable chemical cannot be reduced to permissible safe levels through engineering controls, then the LEAST acceptable exposure control alternative is:
explanation: Administrative controls are methods for controlling employee exposures to contaminants or excess noise by limiting the duration of an individual's exposure by job rotation, work assignment, or time periods away from the contaminant or noise source. Personal protective equipment, such as a respirator, is the last alternative that should be considered to reduce exposures.

question: Safety directors should _______ as many levels of management as possible.
explanation: The fact that the safety director's manager is interested in safety and supportive of the director is more important than the level he/she reports at. It is important that the company's upper management support safety and encourage safety. If the safety function reports at a high level in a company that does not value safety, the level of reporting will not matter. Access to managers throughout an organization will assist the safety director in developing an accepted, consistent, effective safety program.

question: Typically, the product safety engineer is a separate entity of which organization?
explanation: Generally the product safety engineer is a separate entity or of the risk management department organization. For a simple product or process, the product safety engineering organization may be one person. If the organization is large or complex, several people may be needed, even with specializations.

question: The system safety responsibility in many company organizations is placed in the:
explanation: The system safety responsibility in many company organizations is placed in the product assurance department because it is an organizational method of establishing a close relationship among common disciplines such as reliability, maintainability, quality assurance, and human factors engineering.

question: Ozone has a propensity to form free radicals in the body. A toxicologic phrase utilized to describe this phenomena is:
explanation: Ozone's propensity to form free radicals is termed radiomimetic. Webster's 3rd New International Dictionary defines radiomimetic as "producing, especially, biological effects similar to those produced by radiation."

question: Numerous LIFESTYLE factors have been shown to impact the toxicity of chemicals. For example, ________ is known to potentiate both the carcinogenic and noncarcinogenic effects of asbestos.
explanation: Epidemiologic studies have shown that smoking dramatically increases the risk of developing fibrotic lung disease (asbestosis and bronchiogenic carcinoma). Mesothelioma, another tumor type associated with asbestos exposure, has an uncertain relationship to cigarette smoking.

question: Accidental contact with 60 Hz current of 5 to 25 mA can cause the following:
explanation: Victims may become paralyzed with accidental contact with 60 Hz of current in the range of 5 to 25 mA.

question: Electrical shock intensity and effects will depend on the:
explanation: Electrical shock intensity and effects depends on the current path, frequency, and duration.

question: Special hazard terminology has been developed for cranes and derricks. What is the correct term for an undetected hazard, created as a result of the crane's design or by the crane's use?
explanation: A dormant hazard is an undetected hazard created either by the crane's design or crane use. Armed and active are other types of crane and derrick hazards.

question: Which of the following are safety devices installed in boilers to relieve pressure?
explanation: Fusible plugs are designed to relieve pressure and to indicate certain conditions that contribute to low water (which causes pressure build-up). Safety valves will automatically relieve excess pressure or vacuum, that would otherwise damage equipment or result in injury to personnel. The selection, fabrication, installation, testing, and replacement of safety valves and fusible plugs should be in accordance with the ASME code.

question: Which is the preferred guard for power presses performing piercing, blanking, and stamping operations?
explanation: The fixed guard is considered preferable to all other types and should be used in every case unless it has been definitely determined that this type is not at all practical. The fixed guard at all times prevents access to the dangerous parts of the machine. Besides power presses, fixed guards are also on guillotine cutters, drilling machines, gear trains, milling machines, and sheet flattening machines.

question: Guarding by means of a rail enclosure which restricts access to a machine is called:
explanation: Guarding by means of a rail enclosure which restricts access to a machine is called fencing.

question: Which of the following statements describes ergonomics/HFE? I. Engineering something for the population that will use it II. Designing a system so that machines, human tasks, and the environment are compatible with the capabilities and limitations of people III. Designing the system to fit the characteristics of people rather than retrofitting people into the system
explanation: Ergonomics/HFE is a multidisciplinary activity dealing with interactions between man and his total working environment plus stresses related to such environmental elements as atmosphere, heat, light, and sound, as well as workplace tools and equipment.

question: Anthropometry provides the safety engineer with data about:
options: Lifting capabilities of males and females
explanation: Anthropometric data provided specific data about the dimensions of the human body.

question: The most effective time to apply the principles of ergonomics is:
explanation: The most effective use of the principles of ergonomics is when planning a new operation or planning changes to an existing operation.

question: Ergonomics attempts to:
options: Redesign the product to be made more efficiently
Redesign tasks to fit the capabilities of males
Redesign tasks to fit the capabilities of humans
Redesign jobs to reduce the number of tasks required
explanation: The engineer attempts to redesign individual tasks in jobs so that a higher percentage of the human population can safely perform the tasks.

question: It is widely recognized that an important aspect of hand tool use is often overlooked. This aspect is:
explanation: Tenosynovitis is often called a "training" disease. Inexperienced or new workers often exert more force than necessary when using certain hand and power tools. Training in proper methods of tool use and encouraging workers to alternate hands when using selected hand tools (a design consideration, too) is encouraged.

question: What three concepts characterize ergonomics?
options: Human performance, ergonomic design, systems integration
Physical demands, mental demands, emotional demands
explanation: These concepts can be rephrased as work, engineering, and technology management.

question: Good engineering controls for manual materials handling tasks are based on which of the following principles?
explanation: Good engineering controls involve designing the workplace to fit the worker, one of the definitions for ergonomics. The key scientific areas that have been studied for the purpose of developing ergonomic guidelines for workplace design include: anthropometry, biomechanics, epidemiology, and physiology.

question: Work operations, reach, operator's position, and posture are all best analyzed by:
explanation: A human factors engineer would utilize these variables to conduct studies.

question: Which of the following is correct when isolating equipment through lockout/tagout?
options: Pulling a fuse on electrical equipment to guarantee a dead circuit
Disconnecting the main power source to fully disable most machines
Tightly shutting a high pressure valve before starting maintenance work
Physically locking the main power source and labeling it
explanation: The incorrect answers fail to adequately eliminate the hazard. Additional actions require physically "locking out" the energy source(s) and labeling it with a warning tag. 29 CFR 1910.147

question: How does a ground fault circuit interrupter work?
explanation: The GFCI operates by sensing small amounts of current going to ground. There are various types of GFCI's with different tripping currents.

question: After a recent hazardous materials spill of hydrochloric acid, you have been asked to analyze the contents of a catch basin in which some of the spilled acid was collected. After collecting a 65 mL sample from the catch basin, you precisely separate the samples into two 30.0 mL pipettes. Next, you test the remaining 5 mL with PH paper and see that it clearly indicates a pH of around 1. You decide to perform an acid/base titration to determine the precise molarity, or molar concentration of the material in the catch basin. You prepare a 0.100 Molar solution of sodium hydroxide and titrate both of your 30.0 mL samples. The first sample requires 50.55 mL of sodium hydroxide for neutralization, and the second sample requires 50.45 mL. What is the molarity of the hydrochloric acid in the catch basin?
options: the pH paper indicated that the material in the catch basin is actually basic
explanation: First of all, the indication of 2 on the pH paper implies an acidic liquid; therefore, an acid/base titration using sodium hydrochloric acid is appropriate. Sodium hydroxide and hydrochloric acid neutralize one another on a one-to-one basis (the one H+ ion from HCI reacts with the one OH- ion in NaOH, and the one Na+ ion in NaOH reacts with the one CI- ion in HCL). Because of this one-to-one relationship, we can determine the molarity by using this simple identity: M1V1 = M2V2. M1 is 0.100 M of which 50.5 mL (average) was used to neutralize 30.0 mL (V2) of acid of unknown molarity (M2). (M1V1)/V2 = M2 (0.100 M * 50.5 mL)/30.0 mL = M2 = 0.168 M

question: A design which allows the system to function safely until corrective action is possible is called:
explanation: Fail-operational is a design which allows the system to function safely until corrective action is possible.

question: When derating an electronic part, which of the following techniques is not appropriate?
explanation: Decreasing the MTBF is not an appropriate technique for derating an electronic part.

question: The scientific study of how, when, where, and why an illness distributes itself over time in a population describes:
explanation: Epidemiology is a science that investigates the distribution and causes of disease. Epidemiologists study the interplay between the physical environment, biological effects, and social phenomena that relate to human health and illness in the workplace.

question: A group of foundry workers are exposed to an air temperature of 105ºF. Which control would be least appropriate?
explanation: The principal heat load in a foundry is radiant. It is highly unlikely that foundry air will have much moisture. All other methods may have some net benefit.

question: TLV's for gases and vapors are estimated on what unit basis?
explanation: TLV's for gases and vapors are expressed in parts per million, which is a volume/volume ratio, and milligrams per cubic meter, which is a weight/volume ratio.

question: It is necessary for a maintenance worker to enter a confined space where a potential atmosphere immediately dangerous to life or health (IDLH) may be present. Which of the following respirators should the worker use?
options: NIOSH-approved full face chemical cartridge respirator with cartridges rated for the chemical hazard
NIOSH-approved full face demand SAR (Supplied Air Respirator)
NIOSH-approved full face pressure demand SCBA (Self Contained Breathing Apparatus)
NIOSH-approved half face cartridge respirator with HEPA cartridges
explanation: A pressure demand SCBA or pressure demand SAR is required in a known or suspected IDLH atmosphere. A demand SAR may sometimes allow contaminants to be sucked into the mask which may have a negative pressure with respect to the outside atmosphere. A pressure demand SCBA constantly supplies air to the face piece (to ensure that a negative pressure is never experienced inside the face piece). Cartridge respirators are not permitted in known (or suspected) IDLH atmospheres. 29 CFR 1910.134 (d)(2)

question: The basic safety precaution for people who work in confined spaces or in dangerous atmospheres is:
options: Use of safety harnesses and life lines
explanation: The basic safety precaution for people who work in confined spaces or in dangerous atmospheres is the "buddy system". With the buddy system, no worker enters a dangerous atmosphere until someone else has been designated to take responsibility for his/her safety. While one worker goes into a confined space or other dangerous area, the buddy stays in a safe place nearby, alert at all times for danger and ready to act in an emergency. (Usually the buddy is suited up in protective equipment, as is the worker, ready to help the worker out in case of trouble).

question: A mechanical filter respirator is designed to prevent entrance of __________ into the respiratory system.
explanation: Mechanical filters can only remove particles, they cannot remove gases or vapors.

question: Air-purifying and atmosphere-supplying are:
explanation: Respirators can be placed in two categories: a) air-purifying, and b) atmosphere- supplying. Most air-purifying respirators use chemical cartridges to remove contaminants from the outside atmosphere to a concentration acceptable for breathing. Atmosphere- supplying respirators include SCBA and SAR. These respirators have an independent supply of breathable air for the respirator-wearer. There is no such thing as an OSHA-approved respirator.

question: Barrier creams:
options: Reduce contact of potential irritants with the skin
Are preferred to gloves in most cases
explanation: Barrier creams, as their name implies, form a protective barrier between the skin and the chemical. They are not neutralizing agents for chemicals.

question: In which of the following situations may an air-purifying respirator be worn safely?
options: Odor threshold is greater than the allowable level
Odor threshold is equal to the allowable level
Odor threshold is less than the allowable level
Odor threshold is at least 4 times the allowable level
explanation: To wear an air purifying respirator safely, the worker must be able to detect the material at a safe level. If the odor threshold is greater than the allowable level (e.g., the odor threshold is 20 ppm, while the allowable level is 10 ppm), the worker will not know the material is getting through until PEL/TLV levels are reached or exceeded.

question: The risk of developing active pulmonary tuberculosis is substantially increased by which of the following?
options: Exposure to free crystalline silica dust
explanation: Exposure to free silica dust is a risk factor for pulmonary tuberculosis. The fibrosis caused by the silica may make the lung more susceptible to tuberculosis.

question: Which of the following would be most effective in reducing dermatitis in electroplaters?
explanation: The best method of protecting oneself from dermatitis is to prevent all contact with the offending agent. Therefore, gloves is the best answer.

question: When an internal explosion occurs, it causes the shape of the enclosure to change from:
explanation: When an internal explosion occurs, it causes the shape of the enclosure to change from rectangular to elliptical. Adequate strength is one requirement for the design of an explosionproof enclosure; a safety factor of 4 is generally used. To prevent failure of the enclosure, openings are designed to relieve the pressure of the expanding gases.

question: You suspect that a worker's exposure has exceeded the TLV-C for a certain chemical. Unfortunately you do not have a device to measure instantaneous exposures. You do have a longer term measurement device. What do you do? Note: Substance does not cause an immediate reaction.
options: Take an 8-hr sample and back calculate
Take as short as sample as possible
Do not measure and assume the TLV-C was exceeded
explanation: If instantaneous monitoring is not feasible, then the TLV-C can be assessed by sampling over a 15-min period - except for those substances that may cause immediate irritation when exposures are short. ACGIH TLVs and BEIs

question: Pressure testing is a potentially ___________ test.
explanation: Pressure testing may actually destroy the object being tested.

question: How many footcandles of illumination are necessary for work that requires fine assembly?
explanation: 500 footcandle is necessary for the performance of visual tasks of low contrast and very small size over a prolonged period of time (e.g., fine assembly, very difficult inspection, etc.). 5 footcandles is very low light, and is not appropriate for most working environments. 50 footcandle is a typical office environment lighting level, and 5,000 footcandle is well beyond the lighting necessary for the task described.

question: As a safety professional, you are asked to provide guidance in the layout of a 5,000 square-foot, high-hazard facility to be occupied by up to 15 laboratory scientists. The expected configuration of the process equipment presents the need for a dead end corridor in the means of egress arrangement. Based on NFPA 101 (Life Safety Code), what will be your suggestion regarding the maximum permitted length of the anticipated dead end corridor?
explanation: Dead ends are not permitted in high hazard occupancies with an area of more than 200 square feet or an occupant load of more than 3 people. NFPA 101 7.11.4 (Life Safety Code)

question: Delegation of authority and chain of command are characteristic of a:
explanation: The formal structure has a system of objectives that defines roles and responsibilities of the participants. Delegation of authority means authorizing individuals within the structure with defined rights and responsibilities resulting in a "chain of command".

question: All have been identified as "megatrends" by John Naisbett EXCEPT:
options: Transition from industrial to information society
explanation: Naisbett predicted a number of changes including the movement from centralization to decentralization in government and business.

question: Heinrich's domino theory of accidents includes:
options: Social, fault, unsafe act, accident, injury
explanation: Heinrich's domino theory involved social, fault, unsafe act, accident, injury.

question: An effective fire loss control program must include objectives that prevent loss of life and personal injury, prevent inception of fire, protect property and:
options: Incorporate the use of fire resistive building materials
Effect controls that limit the fire load (amount of combustibles)
explanation: In any fire loss control program there is a necessity for a plan that protects against a business interruption. Generally, there is a condition of insurance that you reduce the loss resulting from a business interruption by resuming complete or partial operations on the fire damaged premises and/or making use of other property and materials at other facilities.

question: Political and socioeconomic factors are NOT important considerations in which of the following processes?
explanation: Risk assessment is the scientific discipline involved in characterizing and quantifying the magnitude of potential harm to human health from the presence of a particular agent in the environment. Unlike risk management, risk assessment does not consider economic impact.

question: What does the management term "line function" mean?
options: An employment function for which the enterprise exists
An employment function to support the work for which the enterprise exists
An employment function associated with a manufacturing assembly line
An employment function providing direct supervision
explanation: A line function is a position or role directly involved with the main enterprise of the company. For example, "pigment mixer" would be a line function in a paint manufacturing plant. A staff function, on the other hand, is a position or role that supports the line functions. For example, "security guard" is a staff function for a paint manufacturing plant to ensure the protection of the facilities and people involved in manufacturing paint.

question: A manager who utilizes an external reward and punishment system to affect performance is a _________ manager.
explanation: Theory X holds that people must be motivated to work by external reward and punishment.

question: A manager who utilizes the inherent motivation that is present in all humans is a ________ manager.
explanation: Theory Y managers utilize the goal-orientation of the worker to achieve results.

question: The tendency for an individual who finds himself in a frustrating circumstance and reverts to an earlier form of behavior - such as putting on a temper tantrum - is called:
explanation: Regression is the tendency for an individual who finds himself in a frustrating circumstance to revert to an earlier form of behavior.

question: The tendency for an individual to give up or withhold any sense of emotional or personal involvement in the situation is called:
explanation: Resignation is the tendency for an individual to give up, or withhold any sense of emotional or personal involvement in the situation.

question: Human performance is a function of:
explanation: Human performance is a function of (aptitude + training) * motivation.

question: It is possible to reduce incidents involving human error by:
options: Furnishing workers with personal protective equipment
Providing training and education to workers and line supervisors
explanation: It is generally agreed that the majority of incidents leading to an accident are attributed to unsafe acts rather than unsafe conditions. Although general estimates of the mental and emotional states that cause accidents (like indifference, resentment of authority, disregard of danger, undue haste, anger, impatience, boredom, etc.) are not reliable, there is consensus that effective training and education will prevent many of the human errors (unsafe acts) that arise from mental and emotional states.

question: Workers' compensation represents a significant business expense for employers. To a large extent, employers can influence the cost of this coverage by:
options: Obtaining a low rate prospective experience rating plan
Obtaining a low rate retrospective experience rating plan
explanation: One of the objectives of the workers' compensation system is to encourage safety in the workplace. A credit rating is awarded for better than average injury/illness accident prevention OR a debit rating is charged against the premium for one that is worse than average. Injury rates and the experience modification rating are used to estimate charges. By lowering the experience modification rate one can lower their insurance premium.

question: The acronym CAD/CAM has become very important to manufacturing. What does CAD stand for?
explanation: CAD/CAM stands for computer aided design and computer aided manufacturing. CAD/CAM is used to make manufacturing more cost effective, more time efficient, and to increase overall product quality.

question: A safety professional is asked to evaluate a procedure to address a high pressure steam fitting leak. He or she should ensure that which of the following safety-related caution steps is included prior to repairs being made?
options: Ensure system is shut down, bled, locked out, and tagged out
Wrap line with electrician's tape before making repairs
explanation: The correct caution step is to verify that the system is properly bled and to ensure that the lock out/tagout procedures have been implemented.

question: In organizing and implementing a successful safety and loss control program, it is essential that you:
options: Get top management support and participation
Acquire an environmental health and safety staff
Promulgate a formal safety policy and program
explanation: An effective safety program must begin at the top. Only top management can assign the responsibility for safety and loss control and ensure its performance. Also, top management can implement the controls in the workplace environment along with worker operations that will control accidents.

question: All of the following are examples of staff functions EXCEPT:
explanation: Commanding is a line function and, therefore, not an example of a staff function.

question: A supervisor's job responsibilities include the "3-E's" principles. Which of the following would NOT be included under the "3-E's"?
options: Making sure employees comply with safety rules and procedures
Instructing employees how to work safely
Determining ways for eliminating injury/illness potential from the job
explanation: The supervisor's job involves: ENGINEERING - to determine the most effective way of doing the job and designing the injury/illness potential out of the job. EDUCATION - to instruct the employee in the right method, and through training, improve job skill, knowledge, and behavior. ENFORCEMENT - to ensure the employee follows the prescribed work practice and complies with safety rules and procedures.

question: Within a PERT network, slack time is defined as:
options: The difference between the length of time scheduled for an event and the length of time required for completion
The longest path between critical events
explanation: Slack time within the PERT network is defined as the difference between the length of time scheduled for an event and the length of time required to complete the event.

question: The critical path in a PERT network is defined as:
options: The start time between the longest tasks
The longest time path between beginning and end events
The shortest time path between beginning and end events
explanation: The critical path in a PERT network is the longest time path between beginning and ending events. Critical path defines the sequence of events that control the amount of time needed to complete the effort described by the PERT network.

question: The responsibility for IMPLEMENTING a company's safety and health policy is that of:
explanation: Top management is responsible for setting the company's policy on safety. Top management sets clear-cut restrictions and regulations appropriate to the type of operation, processes, and company size to keep employees at all levels aware of what is required of them in regard to safety. Line and operating management are responsible for implementing this policy and are accountable to top management. Together they are accountable for the safety and health program. The safety professional is the technical expert and can provide advice and counsel on potential implementation plans, but does not generally implement them.

question: Responsibility for safety in day-to-day operations belongs to:
explanation: The line supervisor is the key person who plays an important role as the link between management and the worker. The worker follows the line supervisor's orders, and each worker is responsible for the quality and quantity of their own work.

question: It is generally accepted that the most effective safety program places safety responsibility on the:
explanation: If a supervisor is held responsible for safety performance, he or she will have a personal interest in the program.

question: The success of the system safety effort depends on:
explanation: The success of the system safety effort depends on definitive statements of safety objectives and requirements by the managing activity and their translations into functional hardware and software.

question: Relatively new developments in human resources management include:
explanation: New developments include flex-time (flexible working hours), job-sharing (two or more workers sharing the same job), and work sharing (during downtime, hours are taken away from everyone to prevent layoffs).

question: System engineers seek to drive down the probability of causing a death to users of a system. What is this probability?
explanation: To the average person, accidents with the probability of death of 10-6 or less per person per year are not of great concern to the average person. Hence, many systems safety experts are attempting to design products or processes to a level that is "ten to the minus six" level of performance, or one in a million. NOTE: the probability of being killed in a motor vehicle accident hovers consistently around 10-4.

question: The design, development, and delivery of a new product can be called:
explanation: The design, development, and delivery of a new product can be called a manufacturing system. The system incorporates accidental loss consideration involving system integration of a Machine/Environment (occupational safety) with subsystems pre-production safety and quality reviews (product safety).

question: What is the most critical period in crisis management?
explanation: It is generally considered that the first 24 hours of any crisis are the most critical during the life of the crisis. Management's function is to explain the problem, control rumors, and control panic.

question: What is the value of an investment that will be worth $10,000 after 5 years, given that the interest rate during this period is 10%?
explanation: This question requires calculating the time value of money. Find the present worth of the future investment value as follows: Use the formula: P = F(1 + i)-n P = F(1 + i)-n = $10,000 (1 + 0.10)-5 = $6,209

question: Organizations allocate costs into various categories to aid decision making. Often, these costs are determined as a percent or ratio of manufacturing costs. Examples include raw materials, direct labor, indirect materials, selling costs, distribution costs, and other costs. In calculating return on investment of ergonomic controls, a key expense used to determine the cost-benefit of controls is:
options: Direct costs of accidents inflated over time to determine present value of future workers' compensation injury dollars
The cost of capital associated with purchase and installation of controls
Depreciation costs and pretax operating expenses after controls are implemented
Profit and quality loss as a result of increased absenteeism and poor employee morale
explanation: While all are important, the cost of capital (interest lost from the initial investment) is often ignored. Knowledgeable financial managers will consider the cost of capital when calculating their desired return on investment of a capital expenditure. The challenge of the practitioner is to keep this in mind when determining cost-benefit of controls and, when possible, to quantify productivity efficiency and productivity enhancements to help support action plans.

question: At an annual interest rate of 6.0%, what must the total return on a $50,000 investment be over 3 years to break even?
explanation: This is a compound interest problem. If invested and left alone, the $50,000 would be worth $53,000 after year 1; $56,180 after year 2; and $59,551 at the end of year 3. This is found as follows: $50,000 * 1.06 = $53,000 $53,000 * 1.06 = $56,180 $56,180 * 1.06 = $59,551

question: It is estimated that the total cost to the country from an OSHA regulation is $20 million the first year and $5 million in each subsequent year. If the regulation is estimated to save 5 lives per year, what is the cost per life saved over a 10 year period, not considering the time value of money?
options: One cannot put a value on human life
explanation: To get the cost per life, first calculate the total cost of the regulation. The total cost of the regulation is $20 million for the first year plus (9 * $5 million) for each of the subsequent years. This is $65 million. Then calculate the total lives saved. The total number of lives saved is (10 years * 5 lives per year) = 50 lives. Then divide the total cost by the total lives saved. Thus, the cost per life saved is $65 million / 50 lives = $1.3 million/life.

question: If an investment of $20,000 is made to buy ergonomic tools, and these tools should prevent $10,000 per year in injury-related costs, when will the investment pay for itself, assuming an annual interest rate of 10%?
options: At the end of the first year
explanation: This question requires calculating the time value of money. Find the present worth of the future savings as follows: Present worth of at the end of each year: PW = F (1 + i)-n PW(1) = $10,000 (1 + 0.10)-1 = $9,090.90 PW(2) = $10,000 (1 + 0.10)-2 = $8,264.46 PW(3) = 10,000 (1 + 0.10)-3 = $7,513.15 PW(1) + PW(2) = $17,355.36 PW(1) + PW(2) + PW(3) = $24,868.51 The tools will pay for themselves at some time during the third year. Remember that PW(1) + PW(2) is the present worth at the END of Year 2.

question: A company's finance department requires that all investments pay for themselves within 24 months. You have recommended that $50,000 in material handling equipment be installed to prevent $35,000 in material handling injuries per year. Will the finance department approve your request, assuming an annual interest rate of 8%?
options: Only if the payback is extended to 36 months
explanation: This question requires calculating the present worth of the future savings. That is, what is the present value of $35,000 in loss that will be prevented each year over the next two years required by this finance department. PW(1) = $35,000 (1 + 0.08)-1 = $32,407 PW(2) = $35,000 (1 + 0.08)-2 = $30,006 Total savings after 2 years = PW(1) + PW(2) = $62,413 Since the present value of the savings is greater than the cost, your request should be approved.

question: The finance department requires that all investments pay for themselves in 24 months. You have recommended that $50,000 in material handling equipment be installed to prevent $35,000 in injuries per year. Will the finance department approve your request if the annual interest rate is 12%?
options: Yes if the payback period is extended to 48 months
explanation: This question requires calculating the present worth of the future savings (in this case, the accident costs of $35,000 per year). PW(1) = $35,000 (1 + 0.12)-1 = $31,250 PW(2) = $35,000 (1 + 0.12)-2 = $27,902 Total savings = PW(1) + PW(2) = $59,151 which is STILL greater than $50,000. Therefore, this request ought to be approved, too.

question: In conducting a safety and health audit you ask for workers' compensation cost data. You find the location's experience modification rate to be 0.55. How would you rate the location's safety and health performance with respect to this measure?
explanation: The experience modification is developed from the location's injury/illness frequency and severity rate and the industry rate. If the plant had the same experience as the industry as a whole, the experience modification rate would be 1.0. Since this plant had an experience modification rate of 0.55, it would be considered excellent.

question: Workers' compensation insurance premiums are determined by three rating systems namely, retrospective rating, experience rating, and:
explanation: The first step in the rate making process is to determine a basis for potential loss. With workers' compensation, it is obtained from the payroll (i.e., the number of employees), the number of hours worked, and pay rate. Different types of work entail various degrees of hazard. For example, an office worker will be insured with less risk than a machine operator based on their job classifications. Similar industries have similar or matching classifications. Manual rates are governed by the experience of the industry and are reported annually by insurance carriers.

question: As the manager of the safety and health function, you have access to cost data relating to insurance, medical, wages, and operations. How would you determine the total cost of an injury or illness?
options: Sum the insured and non-insured costs
Combine insurance cost for medical and compensation paid to claimant
Determine the direct cost and multiply it by four
Determine the direct cost and add 25%
explanation: Accident costs include both those that are insured and those that are not insured. The insured costs include medical and compensation costs paid to the claimant by the insurance company. The non insured costs include time lost by others who observed or rendered assistance at the time of the accident, time lost to investigate the accident, time to train a replacement, cost for damaged materials, etc.

question: In one year, a company with 65 employees recorded in their Form OSHA No. 300: 7 injury cases with lost workdays, 2 injury cases without lost workdays, and 2 illness cases without lost work days. The total hours worked by all employees is 130,000. What is the incidence rate of recordable injuries for that year?
explanation: Computation of incidence rate for OSHA-recordable cases: = (No. of recordable cases * 200,000) / Total employee hours = (11 cases * 200,000 hr/yr) / 130,000 = 16.92 cases/yr The OSHA incidence rate is based on 100 employees working 2,000 hours per year. This is the basis for the 200,000 hr/yr in the equation.

question: In one year, a company with 65 employees recorded in their Form OSHA No. 300: 7 lost workdays from injuries, 2 injury cases without lost workdays, and 2 illness cases without lost work days. The total hours worked by all employees was 130,000. What is the incidence rate of lost workday injuries for that year?
explanation: Computation of incidence rate for lost workday cases: = (No. of lost workday cases x 200,000)/Total employee hours = (7 cases x 200,000 hr/yr) / 130,000 hr = 10.77 cases/yr The OSHA incidence rate is based on 100 employees working 2,000 hours per year. This is the basis for the 200,000 hr/yr in the equation.

question: Determine the OSHA-recordable injuries incidence rate for a company if the firm sustained 40 OSHA-recordable injuries in a year in which the 750-person firm worked 1,500,000 hours.
explanation: Computation of incidence rate for OSHA-recordable cases: = (40 cases * 200,000 hr/yr) / 1,500,000 hr = 5.3 cases/yr

question: A worker can perform a certain task in 16 hours. The part of the task the worker can do in H hours is:
explanation: In one hour, the worker can do 1/16 of the total task. In H hours, the worker can do H times (l/16) = H / 16 of the task.

question: Just-in-time (JIT) inventory control seeks to:
options: Minimize the amount of raw material inventory in the facility at any time
Provide line employees with exactly what they need when they need it
Minimize procurement anomalies by establishing standard schedules (based on need) for delivering raw materials/spare parts
explanation: JIT inventory control also helps to reduce overhead costs by reducing storage/warehousing requirements. JIT requires a company to fully understand its production and maintenance system so that optimizations can be made while enhancing quality.

question: Zero-based budgeting means:
options: Developing a budget without considering the value of last year's budget
Creating a budget with no basis
explanation: The essence of zero-based budgeting is starting at "zero", determining which programs are critical, and assessing how much each program actually costs. Last year's budget is not relevant, except as a data point. True zero-based budgeting sometimes shows that some programs are under-funded, while others are not critical or are duplicative.

question: Crew Resource Management (CRM) is a technique to properly use all of the operations professionals on a team to reliably meet mission objectives. It is derived from efforts to make aircraft cockpit crews more team-oriented versus the highly authoritarian environments in which cockpit crews formally found themselves. Of the following, which dynamic human environment is the best candidate for applying the principles of CRM?
options: Offsite incident command staff-onsite incident command staff during an emergency
explanation: Incident command could greatly benefit from applying the principles of CRM. In this environment, all of the incident command professionals have the same goal; however, culture, work habits, and other non-relevant issues can cloud the efficient exchange of information to meet the mission objectives.

question: Theory X management assumes the following:
options: The worker is basically uninterested in work
Worker must be motivated to work
explanation: Theory X management holds that workers must be made to work by a set of external rewards and punishments. Work is not a natural condition.

question: Theory Y management assumes the worker is:
explanation: Theory Y management holds that the worker is interested and motivated to work, as opposed to Theory X.

question: According to contemporary motivation theory, the strongest motivator is:
explanation: Current theory holds that recognition of achievement is the single most important motivator.

question: The LEAST effective means for involving employees in process safety management at a facility is through:
options: Review and input to the program
explanation: An individual reward and discipline program does less to encourage involvement than employee training, committees, and review/input to the program. The latter three allow employees to become informed and involved up-front in decisions that affect their safety and health.

question: Responsibility for safety at the operational level rests with:
explanation: Line supervisors are responsible for safety. Safety management is among the other key aspects of a supervisor's job duties.

question: What functions do corporate safety groups normally NOT perform?
explanation: Corporate safety groups do not normally investigate plant accidents. They frequently review the findings, root causes, and corrective actions generated from a formally conducted incident investigation, though.

question: It can be difficult to get non-users of seat belts to wear them because:
options: The positive consequence of wearing them is future and uncertain
The negative consequences of wearing them are immediate and certain
explanation: Since the positive consequences of wearing seat belts (i.e., prevent injury) is future and uncertain, and the negative consequences of wearing them are immediate and certain (uncomfortable and it takes time), some people may be motivated not the wear them. E. Scott Geller, The Psychology of Safety

question: In behavioral terms, safety management can be considered a continuous fight against human nature because:
options: Positive consequences of unsafe behavior tend to be immediate and certain
Negative consequences of unsafe behavior tend to be uncertain
explanation: The positive consequences of unsafe behavior tend to be immediate and certain, for example, more comfort in not wearing personal protective equipment. In addition, the negative consequences of unsafe behavior, such as having an accident, are uncertain. E. Scott Geller, The Psychology of Safety

question: Why is it a good idea to have a formal safety and health statement of policy?
options: Safety and health should be of primary concern to everybody
It is the starting point for all activities in the safety and health program
It expresses management's attitude toward safety and health
It publicizes the safety and health function
explanation: The formal safety and health statement of policy is an endorsement of top management's commitment and support. It is management's expression of the direction to be followed.

question: A good company safety policy will include all of the following EXCEPT:
explanation: A company safety policy should include: responsibilities, accountabilities, authority, scope, intent, and standards. Though accident history is interesting, a company's safety policy should not dwell on specific past events, but should indicate management's expectations toward future safety-related performance.

question: What is the principle focus of an in-plant medical program?
explanation: The focus of medical programs is on the prevention of occupational disease.

question: The concept of "hierarchy of needs" was developed by:
explanation: Maslow's hierarchy of needs is a critical component of many management theories dealing with human needs.

question: A supervisor's attitude toward safety and health _________ influence on those that he or she supervises.
explanation: A supervisor's attitude is of critical importance to an employee's perception of job safety and health.

question: There are several management theories of motivation, such as Theory X and Theory Y. Which one of the following is NOT true?
options: Theory X - The worker is uninterested and unmotivated to work
Theory Y - The worker is interested and motivated to work
Job Enrichment Theory of Herzberg - Work environment, benefits, and work conditions are all-important
Job Enrichment Theory of Herzberg - Work must be meaningful, must provide recognition, give responsibility, and allow for professional growth in order to motivate the worker
explanation: Job Enrichment Theory of Herzberg - Work environment, benefits, and work conditions are all-important incorrectly identifies Herzberg's Job Enrichment Theory. Herzberg believed that hygiene issues (such as work environment, benefits and work conditions) are necessary before motivation and resultant productivity increases can occur but do not result in motivation. Instead, workers are motivated by work that is meaningful, provides recognition, gives responsibility, and allows for professional growth.

question: The process of determining safety goals, allowing supervisors a chance to perform, providing assistance along the way, and rewarding them according to their progress is known as:
explanation: Safety by Objectives is the process of determining safety goals, allowing supervisors a chance to perform, providing assistance along the way, and rewarding them according to their progress.

question: The key to effective line safety performances are management procedures that fix:
explanation: To be effective, line managers must be accountable for safety performance. Accountability is critical.

question: In the study of traditional management, the term "Span of Control" is used to indicate:
options: The control of many by one
The number of personnel under one supervisor
The number of supervisors that should be in control
The number of supervisors actually in control
explanation: Span of control is the number of personnel that directly report to a single supervisor.

question: The best way to create acceptable new responses to environmental stimuli is to:
explanation: Rewarding a desired response is the best way to encourage the response in the future. Dan Petersen, Safety Management, A Human Approach

question: Which of the following is NOT generally considered positive reinforcement?
explanation: Money, praise, and recognition are forms of positive reinforcement. Dan Petersen, Safety Management: A Human Approach

question: Total quality management (TQM) is an overall commitment to continuously improve quality performance at all levels. All of the following concepts apply EXCEPT:
explanation: Central thinking is not a concept of TQM, although acting as one voice is a concept of TQM.

question: Communication means conveying a message and having it understood. Retention of the safety message is best retained when it is:
options: Presented orally at a rate of 120 words/min
Presented orally at a rate of 450 words/min with body movement
Presented orally at a rate of 120 words/min with visual aids
Presented orally at a rate of 120 words/min with hand and face gestures
explanation: We learn 87% through our eyes and only 7% through our ears. (The remaining 6% balance occurs from other senses, e.g. touch and smell.) Also, there are differences in the rates of listening versus talking and understanding. The average speech rate is 120 words/min, while the rate of understanding is 450 words/min. Adding visual aids to an oral presentation increases the rate of learning and retention of the message presented.

question: A management technique frequently used to explore options and to determine the most remote contingencies is:
explanation: Brainstorming is normally used to fully develop a situation's potential impact. It normally involves several people in a setting designed to draw out all ideas. The ideas are then sorted out and prioritized, and action plans are developed. The unstructured nature of this activity tends to produce more creative ideas. A trained facilitator is often used.

question: The goal of ergonomic/human factors engineering (HFE) may be any of the following EXCEPT:
options: Control stresses affecting worker's psychic comfort
explanation: Ergonomics and human factors engineering in the United States is a multidisciplinary activity. It deals with interactions between individuals and their total working environment, plus stresses relating to such environmental elements as atmosphere, heat, light, and sound, in addition to workplace tools and equipment.

question: One of the current principles of safety management states that the key to effective line safety performance is having management procedures that:
options: Identify and correct unsafe acts and or conditions
Improve worker attitude through education and training
Engineer the hazard out of operations
explanation: Fixing accountability is based on the belief that a line manager will achieve results only in those areas in which he or she is being measured. It has long been felt by professional safety practitioners that the lack of procedures for fixing accountability is safety's greatest failing.

question: One of the principles of safety management states that certain sets of circumstances can be predicted to produce severe injuries. Which of the following circumstances does NOT apply?
options: Accidents occur by chance and cannot be predicted
explanation: The old approach to safety states that once an accident occurs, the severity of injury is dictated by chance. Modern thinking asserts that certain sets of circumstances can be predicted to produce severe injuries. Essentially, we can attack severity directly instead of hoping the severe accident frequency is low.

question: In what ways should safety be managed differently from other company functions?
explanation: The management of a safety program should not differ from any other program - set goals, plan, organize, and execute the plan to achieve the goals. The more the safety program's goals and management style are understood, the more support there will be for the program.

question: What is the key to effective safety management?
explanation: Management must hold supervisors accountable for the unsafe acts committed by the employees they supervise. Accountability produces interest and attention. The result is a more effective program.

question: What is the most important factor in accident prevention?
explanation: The most critical element of any accident prevention program is management support. Without this support the program cannot succeed.

question: Which of the following is the first step in establishing an effective process safety management program?
options: Writing a process safety management program
Establishing a company culture centered on safety
explanation: An effective process safety management program cannot be achieved without first establishing a culture in which safety is a priority and is part of the daily routine of the employee. The hazard analysis and written program will not be implemented, and employee training is not effective without the commitment of the work-force or management.

question: What is the primary reason for a company to institute a fleet safety program?
explanation: The primary reason for a company to institute a fleet safety program is to prevent accidents. As a result of preventing accidents, the number of liability claims will decline and insurance costs should decrease.

question: There are similarities and differences between motor-vehicle safety and industrial safety. Which similarity stands out?
explanation: A statement of management's intent bears the same importance in motor-vehicle accident control as it does in industrial safety. Generally, the policy spells out: Management's statement that safety on the road is important; the company safety program includes the driver; the driver will support the program: and specific safety responsibilities will be assigned to management. Motor-vehicle safety is different from industrial safety in two ways: On-the-road employees are not under constant supervision as they would be in a plant, nor can the driving environment be controlled as effectively as it can be within an industrial setting.

question: A generic process of evaluating competing courses of action by examining the dollar costs of certain abatement actions versus the dollar value of the benefits received is called:
explanation: Cost-benefit analyses are generic processes for evaluating competing courses of action by examining the dollar costs of certain actions versus the dollar value of the benefits received.

question: A measure of the projected dollar loss per unit (or prorated per unit) calculated by dividing the total risk exposure by the total number of units produced is called:
explanation: Unit risk exposure is a measure of the projected dollar loss per unit (or prorated per unit) and is calculated by dividing the total risk exposure by the total number of units produced.

question: The ratio of the risk exposure to the project cost is called:
explanation: Risk exposure ratio is the ratio of the risk exposure to the project cost.

question: If a company is using self insurance to handle risk, the company:
options: Is using the insurance of the employees to cover their risk
Is buying the insurance from a state plan
explanation: The company is not insured and must "fund" their own insurance plan. Self insurance can be used for various types of risks, including worker's compensation, but often the state will require the company to be in good financial health to use this approach, or be bonded for the exposure.

question: Your company manufactures and fills small propane cylinders that are used for torches, camp stoves, and gas-powered lanterns. This product is packaged and distributed to wholesalers and retailers using a combination of transportation options including the company's own fleet of trucks. Your company is responsible for the:
options: Safe containerization of the product shipped via the company fleet. For other modes of shipment, safe containerization is the responsibility of the receiver of the cylinders
Development of safe containers and transportation specifications for the product
Safety of manufacturing, handling, and storage of the product within the facility, and the safe containerization for shipment
Safety of manufacturing. The shipper is responsible for containerization
explanation: The company is responsible for safety in manufacturing and for safe containerization for shipping no matter who does the shipping.

question: As an effective manager, how would you discipline an employee's first minor safety rule infraction?
explanation: The most logical way to deal with a minor rule infraction is some sort of oral reprimand for the first offense. Ignoring it will not cause a change in employee behavior, and a formal reprimand/suspension will likely cause employee dissention.

question: How can a Safety Director LEAST influence line accountability for safety?
options: Put safety in the supervisor's appraisal
Have safety affect the supervisor's income
explanation: All of the above actions will make line supervisors accountable for the safety of their group. However, "putting a supervisor on warning" will cause an adversarial relationship which benefits no one. Once accountability is assigned, improvement in performance is attained more readily. This is true in any line function. Human nature is to pay attention to those things that will be measured.

question: What is the reason that line employees fail to report near misses to supervisors and/or safety staff?
options: Fear of job reprisals from reporting
Fear of peer pressure from reporting
Perception that nothing ever happens to near miss reports
explanation: There are several other reasons why employees do not report near misses. A critical component to an effective loss control program is removing these barriers to reporting near misses. Without effective near miss reporting, a loss control program will have difficulty evolving beyond reactive assessment.

question: In biosafety nomenclature, which agent Class is the most hazardous?
explanation: Biosafety agents range from Class 1 (safest) to Class 4 (most hazardous). Class 5 agents are foreign animal pathogens regulated by the USDA.

question: The color to indicate fire or danger is:
explanation: Red is the color used to denote fire or danger. 29 CFR 1910.144 (a)(1)

question: The basic color used for designating caution is:
explanation: Yellow is the basic color for designating caution. Applications include: aisle marking, "caution" signs, construction tractors and bulldozers, handrails, guardrails, marking for low beams, pipes, and projections. ANSI Z53.1 (1967) 29 CFR 1910.144 (a)(3)

question: The color used to identify physical tripping hazards is:
explanation: Black/yellow is normally used to identify physical tripping hazards. 29 CFR 1910.144 (a)(3)

question: The color generally utilized to denote information is:
explanation: Blue is the color utilized to denote information.

question: What color is generally used to identify moving machine parts?
explanation: Orange is used to identify moving machine parts.

question: What color is generally used to identify safety facts or first aid?
explanation: Green is the universal symbol for safety and first aid.

question: NFPA 704 provides a diamond shaped diagram shown for inherent hazards of a chemical. What does the color blue indicate?
explanation: The color blue stands for health hazard.

question: NFPA 704 provides a diamond shaped diagram shown for inherent hazards of a chemical. What does the color yellow indicate?
explanation: The color yellow relates to a reactivity hazard.

question: NFPA 704 provides a diamond shaped diagram shown for inherent hazards of a chemical. What does the color red indicate?
explanation: The color red indicates a flammability hazard.

question: ANSI A-13.1 provides a scheme for the identification of piping systems. What is the standard color used to identify protective materials?
explanation: Bright blue is the standard color used to identify protective materials.

question: ANSI Z-35.1 provides the specifications for industrial accident prevention signs. What is appropriate to indicate caution against lesser hazards?
options: Light blue background color, black lettering
explanation: Yellow background color with black lettering is appropriate to indicate caution against lesser hazards.

question: ANSI A-13.1 provides a scheme for the identification of piping systems. What standard color is used to identify dangerous materials?
explanation: Yellow is the standard color used to identify dangerous materials according to ANSI A-13.1.

question: Rank the order of traditional hazard warning terms from most serious to least serious.
explanation: Traditionally, there are three levels of hazards: Danger - used where there is an immediate hazard, which, if encountered, will result in severe personal injury or death. Warning - used for hazards or unsafe acts which could result in severe personal injury or death. Caution - used for hazards or unsafe acts which could usually result in minor personal injury, product damage, or property damage.

question: Flammable storage cabinets are normally:
explanation: Most flammable storage cabinets are painted yellow. In addition to being painted yellow they are labeled as Flammable Liquid Storage Cabinets. Some are also red.

question: A fire hydrant painted red on the bonnet and the caps usually indicates that the water flow rate from the hydrant is:
explanation: Red corresponds to less than 500 gpm. Orange corresponds to 500 to 999 gpm. Green corresponds to 1,000 to 1,499 gpm. Light blue corresponds to 1,500 or greater gpm. NFPA 291 - Recommended Practice for Fire Flow Testing and Marking of Hydrants

question: When walking through an office occupancy where the acoustic ceiling was 10 ft, you noticed that the automatic sprinkler heads hung down and were color coded white. What should this tell you?
options: It was an ordinary pendent sprinkler head with an operating temperature of 135ºF - 170ºF
It was an ordinary upright sprinkler head with an operating temperature of 175ºF - 225ºF
It was an intermediate pendent sprinkler head with an operating temperature of 175ºF - 225ºF
It was an intermediate pendent sprinkler head with an operating temperature of 135ºF - 170ºF
explanation: Sprinkler heads that hang down are called "pendent" and when color coded white signify an intermediate rating with a 175ºF - 225ºF operating temperature. NFPA 13 2-2.3.2 (Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems)

question: You are conducting a formal safety inspection of a manufacturing plant with your newly hired safety engineer. During your inspection you observe an employee, without eye protection, working at a bench installing parts. This is not a hazardous operation but it is a posted "Eye Protection" area. Which one of the following is the best course of action?
options: Contact the supervisor and discuss the situation
Test the skills of your new safety professional by letting him or her handle the situation
Confront the employee and determine "Why" eye protection is not being used
Note the discrepancy and do not discuss it until the outbrief when the CEO and the supervisor are both present
explanation: Contact the supervisor who has control of the workplace and discuss the infraction. Communicate this process to the new safety professional.

question: While investigating a serious accident at your facility, you are approached by a journalist with a microphone. You should:
options: Indicate to the journalist that he or she is interfering with an investigation
Stop and talk to the journalist
Direct the journalist to your supervisor
explanation: Journalists want the facts, and if you do not give them factual information, they may theorize and then collect evidence to verify these theories (regardless of the actual facts). In most cases, stopping and spending a minute or two with a journalist and providing him or her with appropriate facts is worthwhile for public goodwill. Passing off a journalist to your supervisor (who probably has fewer facts than you) will not be helpful. For most major accidents, the organization sets up a dedicated public affairs area for journalists. If this is the case, you may want to direct the inquiring journalist there; however, stopping and talking with the lone journalist is still a pretty good tactic.

question: You are the safety manager in a large manufacturing facility. According to company policy, the safety office must approve any activity that is not classified as a routine operation. This has led to the safety office directly approving activities such as truck loading and unloading activities, machine maintenance activities, and custodial activities. Your chief compliant with this policy is that it:
options: Fails to make line managers accountable for their own operations
Requires the safety office staff to be larger than is necessary for a facility of this size
Requires a huge volume of record keeping and auditing
Prevents the safety office staff from focusing on more important activities
explanation: If the "safety office" is the final authority for approving these activities, then line supervisors have little (if any) stake in the work. The principles of accountability cannot be maintained in this environment.

question: The analytical technique called 5-Whys is used to identify:
explanation: 5-Whys is a qualitative analytical technique to identify the root causes of an incident sequence. Once the causal factors (discreet human errors and equipment malfunctions that led to the loss event) are known, a 5-Whys analysis can be performed on each causal factor to determine "Why" the causal factor was allowed to exist.

question: When designing a safety program, it is essential that psychological factors like individual differences, motivation, emotion, attitudes, and ________________ be considered.
explanation: Learning underlies much of what makes for differences and similarities among people. Through learning, people have developed certain kinds of psychological needs, habitual patterns of behavior, ways of reacting to emotion, and the attitudes which brought them into the workplace. It is essential to consider learning because training is a major consideration in safety programming.

question: Non-regulatory consequences of failure to adequately clean-up chemical releases include all EXCEPT:
options: Difficulties in selling the affected property
Reduced collateral value of the property in borrowing situations
Reduced charges to waste disposal budget
explanation: Reduced charges to waste disposal budget is not possible.(Most likely, costs will increase.) Chemical contamination can cause a property to have a negative economic value because the costs of remediation exceed the market value of the property, once remediated. There are legal/regulatory consequences as well.

question: The total value estimated to be at risk as a result of a particular hazard being evaluated is called:
explanation: Total risk exposure is the total number of dollars estimated to be at risk as a result of a particular hazard being evaluated.

question: In assessing risk, one of the analytical techniques used by systems safety is called hazard risk. It is:
options: A means used to identify and measure the hazard
A way to measure potential hazard conditions in the operational phase
A method for calculating the effect of a hazard if allowed to become an accident
The product of hazard severity and hazard possibility of occurrence
explanation: Risk assessment techniques use mainly system-oriented inductive and deductive analyses. The system safety analytical technique called hazard risk is the product of hazard severity and hazard possibility of occurrence (frequency).

question: System availability is defined as:
options: A measure of the degree to which an item is in an operable and committable state.
The hardware which maintains the higher state of productivity
The average degree of reliability needed maintain to status quo
Simply stated by the formula: As = (An)(Aq)(Ai)
explanation: System availability is defined as a measure of the degree to which an item is in an operable and committable state. 661When using a FTA for accident investigation, the accident is the top event. What is a significant reason for using this technique to analyze the accident? 1) All the events are identified 2) The probability that the accident can occur again can be calculated 3) It speeds up the investigation 4) Events that have a zero probability of occurrence are eliminated and the remainder are investigated Ans.4 Often it is important to eliminate those items that did not contribute to an accident so they do not become the focus of investigation and change.

question: Statistically, when several events are independent they:
options: Are not capable of happening at the same time
Are also conditional on one another
explanation: Independent events do not have an effect on the probability of occurrence of any other event. Mutually exclusive events cannot happen together. It is possible that independent events could happen at the same time. 663Two events that cannot occur together are called: 1) Independent events 2) Non-random events 3) Mutually exclusive events 4) Bayseian events Ans.3 Mutually exclusive means that the events cannot occur at the same time. Sometimes this is confused with independent events where one event does not influence another event.

question: Which of the following is not an element of a risk assessment?
explanation: Risk communication is the process of informing the public in a understandable and effective manner of the potential harm from a given exposure situation and/or particular agent. Hazard identification, dose-response assessment, and exposure assessment are all elements of risk assessment as outlined by the National Academy of Sciences.

question: The most appropriate method of analysis to completely evaluate a product in a safety program is:
explanation: While all are appropriate techniques for use in evaluation of a product, no single method can be used to completely evaluate a product.

question: When using system safety techniques to evaluate a product, the most appropriate time to conduct the first analysis is:
options: When the patent is applied for
When the product is first conceived
When the product prototype is developed
When the first products are manufactured but before it is distributed
explanation: While system safety techniques may be employed throughout the manufacturing process, the first analysis should be done at the time the product is conceived. This helps assure that safety is built in from the start and may help avoid costly decisions to re-engineer the product or perhaps even drop plans for the manufacture and distribution of the product.

question: Systems safety techniques employ the use of four categories of analysis. Fault tree analysis is ALWAYS a member of which category:
explanation: A fault tree analysis is an example of a deductive analysis. Deductive analyses start with a top-level event, and logically determine its specific causes. Some FTA's can be qualitative - some can be quantitative. No FTA is inductive.

question: The technique that provides a means for quantitatively evaluating the contribution of human error to the degradation of product quality is called a:
explanation: THERP, a technique for human error predictions was developed by the Scandia Corporation. It provides a means for quantitatively evaluating the contributions of human error to the degradation of product quality. It can be used for human components in systems and can be combined with either failure modes effects or fault tree analysis.

question: In system safety you would use which Boolean gate to connect the causative agents "exothermic reaction" and "outside heat source" to the end product "heat".
explanation: You would utilize an "OR" gate because either an "exothermic reaction" OR an "outside source" will cause heat.

question: In performing a quantitative fault tree analysis, the first step is to define the top event to be investigated by the tree. Then you must gain an understanding of the system. Which of the following is NOT one of the remaining steps?
options: Evaluate the probability of the event chosen as the event to be investigated
explanation: Quantitative data collection is the fourth step, not qualitative data collection.

question: The first step of a system-level fault tree analysis is to define the top event. The failure selected to define the event must be:
explanation: Major system failures are chosen because they will determine key improvements that must be made in system safety. Selection of other, lower-level failures would result in overlooking much of the system for potential failures.

question: The value of  in a fault tree analysis indicates:
options: An event expected to happen during normal use.
explanation: The Greek letter "" represents the probability of a failure of a component of a part of a system. It can also indicate the mean time between failures.

question: The method that uses mathematical simulation, chance processes, and random numbers to determine whether and how frequently the outcome of an event or complex relationship will occur is known as:
explanation: The Monte Carlo Method of simulation is the name of the method used to analyze complex trees. It requires the use of a computer since a reasonably complex tree will require significant calculations to get a reliable answer for the reliability of the main event.

question: The "bathtub" curve is a stress related depiction that describes the relationship between component failure and exposure. Failures occurring during early stages of use occur in the debugging period, which is also called:
explanation: Failures occurring during early stages of use occur during the burn-in period. 675If the mean time between failures of a system is 5,000 trials, what is the reliability of the system over 15,000 trials? 1) 0.05 2) 0.23 3) 0.33 4) 3.00 Ans.1Using the reliability formula: Rt = e-λτ = 1/mean time between failures Rt = e (-15,000/5,000) Rt = 0.0498 676If the reliability of a system over 15,000 trials is 0.05, what is the probability of failure of the system? 1) 67% 2) 76% 3) 95% 4) 100% Ans.3Using the formula: P(f) = 1 - R(t), where: P(f) is the probability of failure and R(t) is the reliability over time. P(f) = 1 - 0.05 = 0.95 or 95% 677The reliability of a component that has two parallel redundant circuits (each redundant system has a reliability of 0.85) is: 1) 1.00 2) 0.98 3) 0.89 4) 0.85 Ans.2The probability of failure of each leg is calculated as R = (1 - 0.85) = 0.15 The probability of a system failure is: Pf = 0.15 * 0.15 = 0.0225 The system reliability is Rs = 1 - 0.0225 = 0.9775 678A system that has multiple units that must operate in order for a given output to occur is said to have: 1) Parallel redundancy 2) Fail safe characteristics 3) High failure rates 4) Series redundancy Ans.4Such a system has series redundancy, and as such, has a low probability for a failure to occur. 679A system with two components in parallel, each with a reliability of 0.70, would have a reliability of: 1) 0.30 2) 0.50 3) 0.70 4) 0.91 Ans.4 Rseries = R1 R2 Rparallel = 1 - (U1 U2) U1 = 1 - 0.70 = 0.30 U2 = 1 - 0.70 = 0.30 Rparallel = 1 - (0.30)(0.30) = 1 - 0.09 = 0.91 If one component fails, another can act as a backup. 680If a system consists of 100 components in series, each with a reliability of 0.9900, the reliability of the entire system is: 1) 0.366 2) 0.634 3) 0.990 4) 0.999 Ans.1In series, multiply the reliabilities of all components. R = 0.99100 = 0.366 366 times out of 1,000 the system would be able to properly perform its function. 681For reliability purposes, adding components in parallel: 1) Decreases reliability in the system 2) Has no effect on reliability in the system 3) Increases the reliability of the system 4) Depends on other subsystems Ans.3Rseries = R1R2 Rparallel = 1 - (U1 U2) U1 = 1 - R1 U2 = 1 - R2 Assume R1 = 0.9 and R2 = 0.8 In a series system the system reliability is: Rs = 0.9 * 0.8 = 0.72 In a parallel system the system reliability is: Rp = - (0.1 * 0.2) = 0.98 682For system (A) to fail, components (B) and (C) which are in parallel, must fail. If the reliability of (B) and (C) are both 0.70, then what is the reliability of system (A)? 1) 0.49 2) 0.51 3) 0.91 4) 0.97 Ans.3In a parallel arrangement the reliability of system RA = 1 - (1 - 0.70) (1 - 0.70) = 0.91 683The reliability of a system is enhanced by adding a component in: 1) Parallel 2) Series 3) Sequence 4) Progression Ans.1The reliability is enhanced by adding a component in parallel. The additional component, which performs the same function within a given system, makes it redundant (or parallel).

question: A switch has 5 components. Each part has a failure rate of 0.3. Failure of any part causes the switch to fail. What in the reliability of the switch system?
explanation: Reliability is defined as (1 - failure rate). The reliability of this system is the product of the reliabilities of the components. R = (1 - 0.3)5 = 0.168 685A switch has 5 components, all redundant to one another. The component failure rates are 1 x 10-3, 1 x 10-2, 1 x 10-1, 1 x 10-3, and 1 x 10-2, respectively. What is the system failure rate? 1) 1 x 10-11 2) 5 x 10-11 3) 1.21 x 10-1 4) 1.21 x 10-2 Ans.1 Given the parallel construction, the total failure rate is multiplicative.
